beats.say: December 2008. In London, a fund manager sits down to write to his investors.
His fund has just lost forty-five point three percent in a year. The world index lost forty point seven. It is the worst year in the fund's table.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.147 · unaudited, before fees

beats.say: And yet, in that same letter, he writes a sentence about somebody else's business. For these high street competitors, the game is over.

scene.q: For these high street competitors the game is over.
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: His name is Nick Sleep. Watch closely. Nothing here is hidden. It just isn't where you are looking.

scene.q: Nothing here is hidden. It just isn't where you are looking.

scene.kicker: NICK SLEEP AND THE NOMAD LETTERS

beats.say: Two shops. The first plays the old game. Prices are high, so every week something goes on sale to pull you through the door.
Sleep's verdict on that game is blunt. Customers are trained to buy on deal, be disloyal and shop around.

scene.find: customers are trained to buy on deal, be disloyal and shop around
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: His one-word summary: Yuck.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: The second shop does something that looks like a mistake. Every time it gets more efficient, it does not keep the saving.

scene.q: The second shop looks like it is making a mistake.

beats.say: In Sleep's words: as the firm grows in size, scale savings are given back to the customer in the form of lower prices.

scene.find: scale savings are given back to the customer in the form of lower prices
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: The customer reciprocates by buying more. That gives the retailer greater scale, and the new savings are passed on as well. A loop. Sleep's word for it: Yippee.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: This, he wrote, is why Costco enjoys sales per foot of retailing space four times greater than run-of-the-mill supermarkets.

scene.q: sales per foot of retailing space four times greater than run-of-the-mill supermarkets
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: Here is the part that should not be possible.

scene.q: Here is the part that should not be possible.

beats.say: Amazon's operating costs per dollar of sales, plus its operating margin, are less than some of its high street peers' costs.

scene.find: plus its operating margin are less than some of its high street peers
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: Read that again. Amazon's costs and its profit, added together, come to less than what those rivals spend just to run the shop.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151 (paraphrased)

beats.say: So in theory, Sleep says, those rivals could price their products at net income breakeven and still not undercut Amazon's prices or profitability.

scene.q: could price their products at net income breakeven and still not undercut Amazon's prices or profitability.
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: Which is the sentence we started with. For these high street competitors, the game is over.

scene.q: For these high street competitors the game is over.
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.151

beats.say: He put the combined US revenues of Amazon's nearest high street rivals at a hundred and fifty billion dollars. And he named firms that had recently gone away. Circuit City. Woolworths. Zavvi.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.152

beats.say: But Sleep did not discover this in 2008. His letters keep going back to an older shop. Wal-Mart.
For forty years, he writes, investors saw the information. On conference calls they cheered: great quarter, Wal-Mart.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2009 · p.162

beats.say: But in his opinion, they incorrectly weigh the information.

scene.q: in our opinion, they incorrectly weigh the information
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2009 · p.162

beats.say: The central engine of success, he wrote, was a thrift orientation fueling growth with the savings shared with the customer.

scene.q: a thrift orientation fueling growth with the savings shared with the customer
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2009 · p.162

beats.say: Instead, investors may place too much emphasis on valuation heuristics, or margin trends. Items he calls transitory and anecdotal.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2009 · p.162–163

beats.say: Put simply: average companies do not do scale economics shared. After all, average companies are more like GM than Wal-Mart.

scene.q: average companies are more like GM than Wal-Mart!
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2009 · p.163

beats.say: A fair objection. If the loop is so powerful, why can't a rival just copy it?

scene.q: Why can't a rival just copy it?

beats.say: Sleep asks himself the same thing, and starts with a confession. He had gone looking for a vivid smoking gun. A brand name, a location, a clever re-insurance contract, or a patent.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.174

beats.say: One big thing is fragile. Take a drug company with a patent. A rival could displace it at any time with a better chemical.

scene.q: A rival could displace it at any time with a better chemical
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.175

beats.say: To better a scale economics business, a rival would have to be superior at, not one thing, but a million little actions.

scene.q: not one thing, but a million little actions
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.175

beats.say: Amazon's shareholder letter that year: four hundred and fifty-two detailed goals, with owners, deliverables and targeted completion dates.

scene.src: Amazon shareholder letter, quoted in the Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.175

beats.say: And one employee initiative, to remove the light bulbs from the vending machines. Really. It saves the firm twenty thousand dollars a year.

scene.lead: remove the light bulbs from the vending machines
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.175

beats.say: Firms that do many things a little better than their rivals, he concludes, are simply harder to beat.

scene.q: They are simply harder to beat.
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 30 Jun 2010 · p.175

beats.say: Now go back to the page we started on. December 2008. The worst year in the table.

scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.147

beats.say: Here is the trick. The moat was never in that year's number. A business running this loop can show thin margins for years, because it chose to. The saving did not disappear. It went to the customer, and came back as scale.

scene.q: The moat was never in the number.

beats.say: It is why Sleep ran his fund the way he did. Few investments, held for long periods. In his words: Zak and I don't want to be busy; we want to be right.

scene.q: Zak and I don't want to be busy; we want to be right.
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.150–151

beats.say: Years later he wrote that the decision not to do something is still an active decision. It is just that the accountants don't capture it.

scene.find: the decision not to do something is still an active decision
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2012 · p.207

beats.say: And the table from that worst year? From September 2001 to the end of 2008, it prints plus one hundred and one point one percent for the fund, unaudited and before fees. The world index: plus seven point seven.

scene.after: Nomad, since inception (10 Sept 2001) to 31 Dec 2008
scene.src: Nomad letter, period ended 31 Dec 2008 · p.147 · unaudited, before fees

beats.say: So the next time you see a shrinking margin, before you call it weakness, ask two questions. Did the company choose it? And where did the savings go?
